Tweedie family for generalised linear models

Source: R/tweedie.R
tweedie_family.Rd

A Tweedie family for stats::glm(), for responses with a mass at zero and a continuous positive part, such as the loss cost (claims amount per unit of exposure) of insurance policies, where most policies have no claim. Its variance is \(\phi \mu^p\) for a power \(1 < p < 2\): a compound Poisson distribution of Gamma claim sizes, the Poisson frequency and Gamma severity of a pure premium in one model.

Usage

tweedie_family(power = 1.5, link = "log")

Arguments

power

The variance power \(p\), between 1 and 2 (exclusive); 1.5 by default. Values near 1 behave like a Poisson model of the claim count, values near 2 like a Gamma model of the amount.

link

The link: "log" (the default, giving multiplicative relativities), "identity", "sqrt" or "inverse".

Value

A family object, as stats::poisson() returns, with the family name "Tweedie" and the power as variance_power.

Details

The family is quasi-likelihood: the coefficients and their standard errors are those of the Tweedie distribution, with the dispersion \(\phi\) estimated from the Pearson residuals, but its density has no closed form, so AIC() is NA. Compare Tweedie models by their deviance, ideally on rows they were not fitted to. The unit deviance is $$2 \left( \frac{y^{2-p}}{(1-p)(2-p)} - \frac{y \mu^{1-p}}{1-p} + \frac{\mu^{2-p}}{2-p} \right).$$

See also

run_shiny_glm_fitting_tool, which fits it from a form.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 2000
age <- sample(18:80, n, replace = TRUE)
claims <- rpois(n, exp(-2 + 0.02 * age))
loss <- vapply(claims, function(k) sum(rgamma(k, shape = 2, scale = 500)), numeric(1))
fit <- glm(loss ~ age, family = tweedie_family(1.5))
exp(coef(fit))
#> (Intercept)         age 
#>  165.849246    1.017522 
summary(fit)$dispersion
#> [1] 80.73336
